policy.note: a derivation must be native source that cites, in the file itself, every retail address the behaviour claims; the auditor reads the file and refuses generated or recompiled sources

scenario_container.statement: the native product reads the retail scenario container with the retail readers' own layout, including their sizer quirks

evidence.claim: 138 of 138 p-code snapshots reproduced byte for byte by the native readers
the world is built from the retail container alone, 230 units of which 95 carry a load-time position, 4 objectives, 1800 deterministic ticks
src/retail_bin_readers.cpp implements the ten readers and cites each retail function it reproduces

unit_construction.statement: a parsed unit record becomes an object whose class comes from its class byte and whose side flags come from the faction table, inserted into a 256-slot table

evidence.claim: the owner-to-consumer chain read instruction by instruction, with the insertion at 0x8226FEC0
the world is built from the retail container alone, 230 units of which 95 carry a load-time position, 4 objectives, 1800 deterministic ticks
src/retail_mission_state.cpp implements the classification, the insertion and the per-faction census

sub_mission_flow.statement: sub-missions are sequenced by index with a step cursor, a start timestamp and a counter condition

evidence.claim: the selector, the step runner and the elapsed test, with Mission 01's four sub-missions and six steps
the world is built from the retail container alone, 230 units of which 95 carry a load-time position, 4 objectives, 1800 deterministic ticks
src/retail_mission_state.cpp implements the sequencer with its bound, its cursor and its elapsed test

mission_counters.statement: mission counters are written by four operations and stamped the first time a counter reaches one

evidence.claim: the single writer, its four-entry jump table and the 232 OrderFlag orders of Mission 01
the world is built from the retail container alone, 230 units of which 95 carry a load-time position, 4 objectives, 1800 deterministic ticks
src/retail_mission_state.cpp implements the four operations in retail's compute-store-then-stamp order

mission_state_machine.statement: the mission runs on the hierarchical state machine the retail manager carries: a transition exits up to the common ancestor and enters down to the target, over the tree the binary declares

evidence.claim: 36 states, 36 parent edges, no cycle, one root, depth 6, and 0x822E7760 writing state code 8 on its entry branch
the ported tree re-measured from the compiled table and the transition order checked step by step rather than by its result
plan_transition implements 0x8219AD20's exit-then-entry order and the table carries the 36 handler addresses with their superstates

mission_area.statement: the mission area is a horizontal rectangle normalised min/max per axis, selected by game mode from the scenario's area records and tested on a position's x and z only

evidence.claim: the predicate reads components 0 and 2, the normaliser writes min and max per pair, and the installer refuses kind 2

the ported normaliser, predicate and selector run against the retail scenario; Mission 01 declares no slot-6 record, and cycle 1121 found where its rectangle does come from - each sub-mission's tag-0 step calls FUN_82268B28 at 0x8226E2A8 - correcting cycle 1117's reading that the static fallback was the path taken
normalise_area, area_contains and select_mission_area implement the three functions and cite them

playable_session.statement: the product's own session loop - input, camera, HUD - runs on the world built from the retail container, with no manifest anywhere on its path

evidence.claim: the loader's sequence read off its own instructions: read the container, publish it at context+0x264, then size the counter table, the sub-mission timestamps and the faction census from the slots it just published

1800 fixed ticks over the world the container built: 230 units, the player the faction switch classified, the camera at the runtime's fixed offset, deterministic across runs and different under a different input stream
the HUD over the retail-built world once the script has run out: outcome panel shown, 4 of 4 sub-missions complete, 230 units still active, 95 of them carrying a load-time position
the numbers the test asserted before either image was written - two captures at tick 900 and tick 1800, differing colour hashes, 1276 and 1521 HUD pixel writes, no fixture

src/retail_session.cpp opens the payload, follows 0x8219BDD8's order through build_retail_world, takes the player from the class-0 Set on the campaign arm (820a72c0, 0x820A72EC, vtable 0x820568D4 = CAce6UnitPlayer) and from category 2 only on the online arm, installs the container's own combat states instead of the developer spawn layout, and draws only the units the container gives a position

mission_completion.statement: the mission reaches its debrief because the retail sub-mission script ran out, and for no other reason

evidence.claim: the cursor 0x82267370 transcribed instruction by instruction, the state handler 0x822ED708 that calls it on signal -2, the exhaustion branch into 0x82266710 and its write of 1 to context+0x338, and the six-step trace those imply before it was measured

the predicted trace measured at three cadences, identical each time; the debrief reached with 4 of 4 sub-missions behind the cursor; and a session whose script never advances still in gameplay at tick 1800 with nothing completed
src/retail_mission_script.cpp implements the advance in 0x82267370's own order, its three-way entry guard, the payload step-count bound, the exhaustion return and the end code 0x82266710 writes

retail_input.statement: the native product reproduces the controller snapshot NU::Input hands to gameplay -- the axis split, the button edges and the 0x40-byte block the accessor copies -- with every rule read off an instruction, and the retail stages executed on a synthetic device write what the port says they write

evidence.claim: the chain read end to end: the wrapper at 0x823911C0, XINPUT_STATE at device+0x44, the axis table at 0x8201250C, the button edges of 0x8234D378, and the li r5,0x40 memcpy at 0x8234D0A0 whose boundary stops one byte before the kernel structure
the axis split exercised over all 65,536 inputs, the button complement at +0x20 checked as 32-bit, and the decoded halves required to equal split_axis of the raw value beside them
0x8234D110 and 0x8234D378 executed on a synthetic device over 12 cases, 168 fields compared byte for byte against the port, no divergence

include/ac6/retail_input.h carries the derivation and names what is not ported: the wrapper, the two readers, the poll entry as DriverController vtable 0x820124F8 slot +0x10, the axis loop and its table, the button arithmetic, the accessor, the capability map, and the dispatch at 0x82343A30 with 0x82343838's return value

retail_input_record.statement: the native product reproduces the per-controller input record 0x821CAA50 builds -- the fourteen-bit button remap, the two scalar slots and their separate flag gate, and the four axis slots with their negative-zero idle state -- with every rule produced by executing the retail function rather than by reading it, 321 retail vectors reproduced bit for bit, and the same snapshots replayed from a log to the same records and the same digest

evidence.claim: 0x821CAA50 executed to return in 4740 steps under three controller plans; the record base corrected from 0x826EDBA0 to 0x826EDB98, r20 settled at zero from the function and all three of its callers, and all four records shown to be filled from driver-pointer slot 0

321 retail vectors compared bit for bit against build_input_record with no divergence, the named boundaries 0x07FF/0x0800/0x0801 and 0x4000/0x7FFF/0x8000/0xFFFF as separate expectations, and a deterministic replay of the same 321 snapshots -- twice, and across a file round trip -- to digest 0x4b08109c2c631941, with a paired control showing the digest moves for a mapped device bit and does not for an unmapped one

255 executions of 0x821CAA50 driving one axis half at a time -- 108 points on LY+ and every named boundary on the other seven -- all 255 reproduced by the composed rule, which the sweep produced rather than confirmed

include/ac6/retail_input_record.h carries the derivation and names what is not ported: the constant 3 at record+0x98, the zeros at +0x8C..+0x94, and the second normalisation at 0x821CB244 that no input yet found reaches

retail_transform.statement: the native product reproduces the transform kernel 0x822A1E80 and its three rotations in ONE implementation shared by flight orientation and rendered-unit orientation -- the identity basis it copies from .rodata, the three plane rotations each fixing one row, and the composition order f2, f1, f3 which is not the argument order

evidence.claim: 0x822A1E80 read end to end: 40 instructions, no vector arithmetic, three .rodata constants copied to object+0x10/+0x20/+0x30 and three calls, with the two engines agreeing on all 40 instructions
14 retail vectors reproduced, zero-angle cases bit for bit and turned cases within a tolerance that exists only because XMScalarSinCos is not ported

0x822A1E80 and each of its three callees executed on an asymmetric sentinel basis at four angles, twelve rotation cases checked lane by lane against a stated model with a worst deviation of 1.5e-06 and exactly zero at every zero angle

include/ac6/retail_transform.h carries the derivation, states that there is ONE kernel for both paths and why, and names what is not ported: the object's first 16 bytes and the trigonometry of 0x8209CB70

retail_input_binding.statement: the native product reproduces the input binding layer 0x82211C10 -- the deadzone, scale, clamp and sign restoration of one axis, the three-region step, the inversion mask, and the skip that stores NOTHING when the processed value is exactly zero -- reading the record with the same (bit + 3) * 4 rule the retail_input_record behaviour already carries

evidence.claim: 0x82211C10 read whole against .pdata, with the (bit + 3) * 4 record access, the 24-byte descriptor at player + 24*(bit+6), and the three constants -1.0, 1.0 and 0.0 read rather than assumed
boundary tests at the deadzone and threshold exactly and either side, the clamp, both signs and negative zero, with two negative controls that fail on exactly the cases they should
0x82211C10 executed on a synthetic player block and record over 38 cases, both outputs compared bit for bit, including negative zero and the values either side of both boundaries, no divergence
include/ac6/retail_input_binding.h carries the derivation, states why an empty optional is not zero, and records that the layer is table-driven so a port must not hard-code any threshold

retail_slot_repeat.statement: the native product reproduces the slot edge and auto-repeat bank 0x82211988 -- the two edge words, the triggered set that carries repeats, and 32 timer and limit pairs whose initial delay and repeat interval are fields rather than constants -- with equality firing, the reset preceding the add, and a release restoring the initial delay

evidence.claim: 0x82211988 read whole: 32 (timer, limit) pairs from this+0x1060, the delay at +0x1058 and the interval at +0x105C, and the float accumulated into the timers -- so its role is input auto-repeat and not flight integration

boundary tests: equality fires, the reset precedes the add so a fired slot holds the elapsed time, a release restores the initial delay, and the edge words are asserted equal to button_edges' two sets

0x82211988 executed on a seeded object over nine cases with all three edge words and all 32 pairs compared bit for bit; .pdata has no row for this function, so this is the only length-independent check the port has

include/ac6/retail_slot_repeat.h carries the derivation, records that f1 survives 0x82211B40 and 0x82211C10 untouched before reaching 0x82211988, and states that the delay and interval are fields a port must not bake in
